paper: Risk Parity Portfolios with Skewness Risk: An Application to Factor Investing and Alternative Risk Premia (arXiv:2202.10721)
kept: The paper's whole mechanism: asset returns as a 2-component Gaussian mixture under parametrisation (14) (normal regime N(mu,Sigma) with prob 1-pi, jump regime N(mu+mu~,Sigma+Sigma~) with prob pi), risk measured by the 99% expected shortfall UNDER that mixture (eq.4) instead of volatility, the closed-form risk contributions of eq.5 / Appendix A.5 (varpi_i, delta_i, d_x VaR written literally), the risk budgeting portfolio RC_i(x) = b_i ES(x) with b_i = 1/n (ERC) solved by the log-barrier program min ES(y) - sum b_i ln(y_i), x = y/sum(y), long-only and fully invested, with mu = 0 in the allocation - AND the section 4.3 / Appendix A.9 backtest protocol: pi, mu~, Sigma~ held fixed while the NORMAL-REGIME covariance Sigma_t is re-estimated by the paper's preferred FILTERING algorithm (posterior jump probability for every date of the one-year rolling window computed from (mu^_{t-1}, Sigma^_{t-1}), then (mu^_t, Sigma^_t) formed from the window dates with pi^ <= pi* = 30% only, with the A.9 n_t divisor), plus the section 4.1 constraint that an asset whose estimated expected jump is positive carries no jump component; monthly rebalancing on weekly returns, allocated across the five long-only equity risk factors of section 5.1 (size, value, momentum, low beta, quality).
changed: (1) ASSETS: the paper's empirical three-asset mix (US bonds / S&P 500 / short-volatility carry, Jan 2000-Dec 2015) is not reproducible here - no US bond index and no short-volatility carry panel exists in this repository - so the allocated assets are instead the paper's OWN section 5.1 objects, the five long-only equity risk factors (size, value, momentum, low beta, quality), rebuilt as sleeves in the Korean measurement-axis universe; this is why fidelity=adapted rather than faithful. (2) UNIVERSE SUBSTITUTION: measurement axis = all stocks + hygiene (epoch all_hyg_2000_v1); the contract injects that membership into RAWDATA$K200 and the engine filters only on membership, adding no universe rule of its own. The paper documents no universe, exchange, price or liquidity rule at all (section 5.1 delegates to Cazalet and Roncalli (2014)), so there is no paper rule to violate here. The membership test is written as (!is.na(K200) & K200 > 0) | (!is.na(KQ150) & KQ150 > 0) rather than == 1: the NA guard and the > 0 form are defensive code of mine, equivalent to the prescribed K200 == 1 | KQ150 == 1 for the 1/0 flags the contract injects. (3) SAMPLE PERIOD: paper Jan 2000-Dec 2015 -> .RP_START_DATE (2000-01-01) onward, with no date literal in the engine; additionally the first .N_MIN_JUMP = 200 COMPLETE weekly sleeve observations (200/52 = about 3.9 years, longer if weeks drop out per (19)) emit NO rows, because that is the shortest expanding window in which the jump regime has one expected observation. The clock starts not at .RP_START_DATE but at the first month-end at which all five sleeves can be formed (factor-DB availability, (27)(c)-(d)), so the first signal date is roughly 3.9 years after that month - I do not assert a calendar date, the contract's coverage record shows it. The weekly sleeve-return history itself is built only from .RP_START_DATE forward (earlier RAWDATA is never read) so the engine stays inside the axis. (4) JUMP PARAMETERS - PIT FIX: section 4.3 holds pi, mu~ and Sigma~ 'given once and for all, and are set to the previous estimates' (i.e. the full-sample Table 9 estimates) and re-estimates only Sigma_t; PIT C1 forbids full-sample statistics, so mu~ and Sigma~ are re-estimated at every REBALANCING date on an EXPANDING window of weekly sleeve returns ending at that date (minimum 200 weeks) and held fixed between rebalancings. pi itself stays at the paper's calibrated value and is never estimated, as in the paper. (5) FREQUENCY CELL CHOSEN: the paper reports a weekly model (pi=0.5%, Table 9/Table 11) and a monthly model (pi=1.0%, Table 21); I took the WEEKLY cell for estimation (so the section 4.3 one-year rolling window = .N_WIN_NORMAL = 52 weekly observations) with the paper's MONTHLY rebalancing - returns feeding the model are weekly, the allocation and the rebalance are monthly, one signal date per month (last trading day), which puts the run on the harness monthly path (H10). This is the same (frequency, rebalance) cell as the paper's section 4.3 backtest. (6) SLEEVE INTERNALS: the paper gives no construction for its five factor portfolios (it allocates across given factor portfolios / indices), so our fixed axis supplies them - top .TOP_N_SLEEVE=5 names by Z_Score_Aligned, equal weight inside the sleeve, 5 sleeves x 5 = union at most 25 names (axis cap); final stock weight = sum over sleeves of x_sleeve / members_in_sleeve, aggregated across sleeve overlap and renormalised to 1. (7) FACTOR VALUES ARE TRANSFORMED, NOT RAW: Z_Score_Aligned is a cross-sectionally winsorized, z-scored, direction-aligned and re-standardised-to-sd-1 value (C13/C15 via load_month_factors), whereas the paper's factor inputs are factor-portfolio return series; the ranking therefore runs on transformed values. (8) SLEEVE LEG DIRECTION IS NOT FIXED - IT IS SET BY THE CONNECTOR'S ic_sign: the paper's five legs are direction-fixed long-only factors ('size, value, momentum, low beta and quality'). In this repository the only admissible factor value is Z_Score_Aligned (PIT C13 forbids any engine-side NEGATE_FACTORS / FLIP_SIGN), and Z_Score_Aligned = Z_Score * ic_sign where ic_sign is, in order of precedence, (a) the sign of the expanding-window mean IC available at the signal date (36-month burn-in, Usable_Date <= sig_date), (b) the registry direction when IC is unavailable, (c) +1 otherwise. The sign is therefore re-evaluated at every signal date from realised IC and CAN invert: in a period whose realised IC is positive for beta, the D02_Beta sleeve is a HIGH-beta sleeve rather than the paper's 'low beta' leg, and likewise S01_Size can become a large-cap sleeve. Registry directions (S01_Size higher_better, D02_Beta lower_better, M01/V01/Q01 higher_better) agree with the paper's legs but are only the SECOND branch, not a guarantee. This deviation is imposed by the harness rule, not chosen, and it cannot be removed inside the engine; it is declared instead of being asserted away (the previous rejected engine declared the registry direction as a guarantee - that declaration was wrong). (9) EXPECTED RETURNS: mu = 0 in the allocation per section 4.2 ('we assume that the expected returns mu_i are equal to zero ... in order to limit the in-sample bias') and the section 4.3 footnote ('the ERC portfolio is calculated by considering that the expected returns in the normal regime are equal to zero'), while mu_2 = mu~ keeps the skewness channel (gamma_1 != 0 iff x'mu~ != 0). The filtering recursion separately uses its own mu^_t for the posterior densities, exactly as A.9 step 2 specifies - the two are different objects and are not mixed. (10) SECTION 4.1 ZERO-JUMP CONSTRAINT - IMPLEMENTED ON THE SIGN ONLY, AND RE-EVALUATED EVERY REFRESH: the paper's final model imposes 'the constraint that bonds have no jump component, because the previous estimations suggest that the expected jump is positive for this asset class. Moreover, it is not statistically significant' (Table 9 and Table 21 show the bonds row as mu~ = 0.00, sigma~ = 0.00, rho~ = 0.00; Tables 15-20 are the unconstrained estimates in which the bonds mu~ is indeed positive). The engine applies the same rule mechanically: any sleeve whose estimated mu~_i is POSITIVE has its whole jump component zeroed (mu~_i := 0 and row i and column i of Sigma~ := 0, which is what the Table 9 bonds row is). Three parts of the paper's procedure are NOT reproduced: (a) the statistical-significance half of the paper's justification is not tested, so the constraint fires on the sign of mu~_i alone; (b) the paper re-estimates the constrained model by maximum likelihood ('The EM algorithm can no longer be applied due to the constraints'), whereas here the constraint is enforced inside a SECOND EM pass (the constraint set is fixed from an unconstrained first pass, then the M-step zeroes those components every iteration), followed by a final hard enforcement with no further re-estimation if any mu~ component is still positive; (c) the paper fixes the constrained asset once for the whole backtest, whereas here the constraint set is recomputed at every refresh, so a sleeve may carry a jump component in one month and none in the next. Consequence to note for the audit: because of this constraint mu~ <= 0 componentwise always, so a positive x'mu~ (which would make the portfolio skewness positive and LOWER its ES) can no longer arise. In the limiting case where ALL five sleeves are estimated with a positive mu~, the jump component vanishes entirely (mu~ = 0 and Sigma~ = 0), the mixture degenerates to a single Gaussian, the A.9 posterior becomes pi^ = pi = 0.5% for every date so no week is excluded, and that month's allocation is the Gaussian-ES ERC portfolio - a consequence of the paper's own constraint, not a fallback. (11) Sigma~ IS PROJECTED ONTO THE PSD CONE INSIDE EVERY M-STEP: parametrisation (14) makes Sigma~ a covariance matrix ('This parametrization ensures that the estimated model is a Gaussian mixture model with a jump component, and not a two-volatility regime model'), so the unconstrained difference Sigma_2 - Sigma_1 is projected by clipping negative eigenvalues at zero and component 2 is rebuilt as Sigma_1 + Sigma~ before the E-step. The projection mechanism is mine; the constraint it enforces is the paper's. With only about 1 to 6 effective jump observations the raw difference is generally indefinite, and in practice the projection can leave Sigma~ near zero so that skewness enters mainly through x'mu~ (exactly the paper's stated condition for non-zero skewness). (12) EM DETAILS THE PAPER DOES NOT SPECIFY: pi is held fixed and never updated in the M-step (the paper's A.3 M-step does update it, but section 4.1 fixes pi by the expected-drawdown calibration); initialisation is DETERMINISTIC - the k2 = max(.EM_INIT_JUMP_OBS = 6, floor(pi*T)) worst equal-weight weeks seed the jump component - so there is no set.seed, no RNG, no ensemble and no burn-in draw; iteration cap .EM_MAX_ITER = 200; convergence tolerance .EM_TOL = 1e-8 on the maximum posterior change; the loop breaks early and KEEPS THE LAST VALID M-step parameters if the jump posterior mass falls below .EM_MIN_JUMP_MASS = 1.0, if the normal-regime mass falls below .MIN_OBS_COV = 6, if a weighted covariance is undefined, or if the Cholesky in the log-density fails despite the ridge; and .sk_em returns nothing at all (so the jump parameters are simply not refreshed that month and the previous ones stay in force) unless the window has at least k2 + .MIN_OBS_COV observations. None of these safeguards is in the paper, and the jump-mass floor can stop the EM after a single M-step when the posterior jump mass is thin, which at pi = 0.5% is the normal case. (13) A.9 n_t FLOOR: A.9 step 3 divides by n_t = the number of non-jump dates in the window and places no floor on it. The engine requires n_t >= .MIN_OBS_COV = 6 (the minimum for a non-singular 5x5 covariance); if fewer dates survive the jump filter, the previous estimates (mu^_{t-1}, Sigma^_{t-1}) are carried into week t unchanged. Not in the paper. (14) A.9 WARM-UP: A.9 presumes (pi, mu~, Sigma~) are already given. Before the first EM estimate exists (weeks 53 to 199) there are no jump parameters, so no posterior can be computed and NO date is excluded - the filter update degenerates to the plain rolling ML mean and covariance of the 52-week window. This extends the paper's own initialisation ('The only difficulty is the initialization of the covariance matrix. For that, we consider that there is no jump in the first rolling window') through the warm-up; week 52 itself is initialised exactly that way ('To initialize the algorithm, we can use the traditional Gaussian estimates'). No month in this span emits rows anyway, but the recursion state it produces is what the first live month starts from. (15) A.9 THRESHOLD BOUNDARY: A.9 step 3 keeps dates with 1{pi^_{t-s} <= pi_bar} while section 4.3 declares a jump by J_t = 1 <=> pi^_t >= pi*. The engine implements A.9 literally (keep = pi^ <= .PI_STAR, with pi_bar = pi* = 30%), so the boundary value pi^ = 30% is kept rather than excluded. Measure-zero, declared for completeness. (16) ML ROUTE FOR Sigma_t NOT IMPLEMENTED: section 4.3 offers two estimators for the normal-regime Sigma_t - rolling-window mixture maximum likelihood with (pi, mu~, Sigma~) fixed, and the filtering method of A.9. The paper states the ML route 'is not our preferred approach' and reports the filtering allocation (Figure 17) as the result, so only the filtering route is implemented; the ML comparison (Figure 23) is omitted. (17) dt = 1: Remark 1 sets dt to one, so every weekly quantity is in native weekly units - Sigma_t, mu~ and Sigma~ are weekly covariances/means and the paper's annualised parameter tables (Tables 8-21) are not reproduced or compared. .DT enters the A.9 posterior formula explicitly to keep the correspondence with the paper's phi_n(y; mu^dt, Sigma^dt) visible. (18) REFRESH CADENCE AND ORDERING: mu~ and Sigma~ are refreshed once per rebalancing week, AFTER that week's A.9 filter update. So Sigma^_t at a signal date was filtered with the PREVIOUS month's jump parameters while the allocation at that date uses the freshly refreshed ones (both estimated only from data up to that week). The ordering is deliberate: refreshing first would let the EM see week t and then classify week t with parameters that already contain it (C3 flavour). The paper has no such ordering question because its jump parameters never move. (19) MISSING AND NON-FINITE HANDLING: daily returns with non-finite Ret are dropped before weekly compounding; Ret is taken from RAWDATA$Ret when that column exists and is otherwise computed per ticker as Close/shift(Close, .RET_LAG_DAYS)-1; a stock absent for an entire week contributes nothing to that week's sleeve mean (mean over available members, na.rm = TRUE); a week enters the estimation panel only if ALL FIVE sleeves have a value (complete.cases), incomplete weeks being dropped - which lengthens the warm-up of (3) in calendar time; there is no nafill, no locf and no pre-listing constant extension. (20) WITHIN-SLEEVE REBALANCING OF THE ESTIMATION SERIES: a sleeve's weekly return is the equal-weight mean of its members' compounded weekly returns, i.e. the sleeve is re-equal-weighted each week inside the month rather than bought-and-held; this affects only the model's input series, not the traded portfolio, which is held per H5. (21) DETERMINISTIC TIE-BREAK: sleeve ranking orders by (-Z_Score_Aligned, Ticker) so score ties resolve reproducibly. (22) OPTIMISER, AND NO MODEL-SWITCHING FALLBACK: the paper names the program (section 3.3.2) but not the algorithm, so it is solved by BFGS on the log parametrisation y = exp(z) with the analytic gradient RC(exp z) - b (the first-order conditions ARE the risk budgeting equations), .OPT_MAXIT = 500, .OPT_RELTOL = 1e-12, infeasible steps returning .OPT_PENALTY = 1e10, up to .OPT_RESTARTS = 2 starting points (inverse-volatility, then equal weight), each rescaled so ES(y0) = 1; a solution is accepted only if max|RC_i/ES - b_i| <= .RC_TOL = 0.02. If no start is accepted the month emits NOTHING (the harness then carries the previous holdings forward, H5). There is deliberately NO inverse-volatility fallback: substituting volatility-based weights would silently blend in the very comparison portfolio the paper argues against. (23) GRADIENT GUARD IS NOT A SILENT ZERO: if the expected shortfall or its gradient is not evaluable at a trial point (VaR root-find failure, or varpi_1 + varpi_2 < .VARPI_FLOOR = 1e-12), the gradient function raises and that optimisation attempt is abandoned - it does NOT return a zero vector, which would have made BFGS treat the point as a stationary point and stop there (that silent zero was in the previous rejected engine and is removed). The VaR bracket also widens geometrically (.VAR_BRACKET_GROWTH = 2, up to .VAR_BRACKET_TRIES = 10 times from |mu| + .VAR_BRACKET_MULT = 20 sd) so that failure is essentially unreachable; the tail equation is continuous and strictly decreasing with limits 1 and 0, so a root always exists. (24) OTHER NUMERICAL GUARDS NOT IN THE PAPER: relative diagonal ridge .EM_RIDGE = 1e-6 on the EM component covariances and .COV_RIDGE = 1e-8 on every filtered covariance (Sigma^_t and Sigma^_t + Sigma~); variance and denominator floor .NUM_FLOOR = 1e-10 used as sqrt(max(x'Sigma x, floor)) and pmax(diag(Sigma), floor); uniroot tolerance .VAR_TOL = 1e-10. (25) COVARIANCE DIVISOR: A.9 step 3 divides the covariance by n_t (maximum-likelihood divisor, not n_t - 1); the engine uses crossprod/nrow accordingly, including for the Gaussian initialisation. (26) LOG-SUM-EXP STABILISATION: posteriors are computed as exp(a2-m)/(exp(a1-m)+exp(a2-m)) with m = max(a1,a2); algebraically exact, it only prevents overflow when a near-degenerate jump component produces very large log-densities. (27) MONTHS WITH NO OUTPUT - THE HARNESS THEN CARRIES THE PREVIOUS HOLDINGS FORWARD (H5), with no rebalance that month: (a) fewer than .N_MIN_JUMP = 200 complete weekly observations; (b) the universe at that month-end has fewer than .MIN_SLEEVE_NAMES names; (c) load_month_factors errors, returns zero rows, or its factor_db_asof_date is NA or LATER than the signal date (explicit PIT guard); (d) ANY one of the five sleeves has fewer than .MIN_SLEEVE_NAMES = 3 ranked candidates, in which case the whole month is skipped rather than allocated over four sleeves; (e) no jump parameters are in force yet (no EM pass has ever succeeded); (f) the risk budgeting program is not solved to .RC_TOL from either start, or the gradient is not evaluable; (g) every aggregated weight is non-positive; (h) a month-end whose last completed week index is below .N_WIN_NORMAL = 52 (no rolling window yet). (28) ZERO-WEIGHT NAMES DROPPED: names whose aggregated weight is zero or non-finite are removed before the final renormalisation, so a sleeve that receives exactly zero allocation contributes no holdings that month (and the month is skipped entirely if that leaves nothing). The paper, allocating over five always-present assets, has no such case. (29) SIGNAL_BREADTH is deliberately NOT emitted (this is a PORTFOLIO-only engine), so per H3 the measurement is not truncated by the breadth rule. (30) DEDUP: dedup = FALSE is passed explicitly; the five factor ids sit in distinct registry dedup clusters (S01_Size = DUPC-030 partners L26_Log_MktCap / S02_Float_Size; M01_Mom_12_1 = DUPC-032 partner M13_VolAdj_Mom; D02_Beta = DUPC-011 partners D10_Blume_Adj_Beta / D11_FP_Beta / D18_BAB_Rank / D19_EW_Beta_63 / D20_EW_Beta_126 / D28_Unlevered_Beta / D31_Relative_Beta / MK01_CAPM_Beta; V01_BM and Q01_GPA carry no dedup declaration) and no used id is a declared partner of another used id, so no cluster double-votes. (31) FACTOR WINDOWS COME FROM THE REGISTRY, NOT THE PAPER: 252-day momentum with a 1-month skip, 252-day rolling CAPM beta, quarterly+45d / annual 3/31 fundamental availability - the paper specifies none of these because it allocates across already-built factor portfolios. (32) COVERAGE FLOOR: coverage_min = .FDB_COVERAGE_MIN = 0.05 (the connector default) is passed explicitly; the paper has no coverage requirement. (33) COMPARISON PORTFOLIOS OMITTED: Table 11's minimum-variance, minimum-ES and Gaussian-model portfolios are diagnostics, not the framework portfolio; only the mixture ERC risk budgeting portfolio is implemented. The thresholding jump detector (A.7/A.8) is likewise omitted because the paper rejects it in the multivariate case ('the thresholding approach is no longer valid in the multi-dimensional case ... we prefer the filtering approach'). (34) COSTS: commission_paper = null because the paper mentions transaction costs only as motivation (section 5 opening) and never models them, so only the harness 15bps grade board applies (H7). (35) SINGLE-PASS UNIVERSE MATERIALISATION: axis membership is extracted once for the whole month-end grid and keyed, rather than re-scanned per signal date; speed-only change with identical values. (36) TWO MONTH-ENDS SHARING ONE WEEKLY OBSERVATION: the allocation at a signal date uses the last weekly observation that closed at or before it. If the weekly panel has a gap (weeks in which one of the five sleeves had no value are dropped, changed (19)), two consecutive month-ends can map to the same last available week; both then receive the same sleeve weights, computed from that one information set, while the stock-level composition still differs because each month's sleeves are formed at its own month-end. The paper, with an uninterrupted weekly index series, has no such case. (37) STALE FACTOR PANEL IS ACCEPTED, NOT DETECTED: load_month_factors falls back to the closest EARLIER monthly parquet when the signal month's file is missing (connector lines 322-330). That is PIT-safe, and the engine's guard only rejects a panel whose factor_db_asof_date is NA or later than the signal date - it does NOT reject an older panel. So in a month with no factor file the sleeves are formed from an older cross-section rather than skipped. Connector behaviour, accepted by the engine, not in the paper. (38) WEEK BLOCKING AND AS-OF LAGS ARE NAMED CONSTANTS: .WEEK_LEN = 7 (days per ISO week block), .ASOF_LAG_DAYS = 1 (composition as-of = the latest month-end STRICTLY before a week's first trading day) and .RET_LAG_DAYS = 1 (daily return lag in the Close fallback) replace inline literals; values unchanged, listed in constants. (39) EXISTENCE CONDITION NOT TESTED AT RUNTIME: Theorem 1 requires alpha >= max(alpha^-, lambda) for the RB portfolio to exist and be unique, and the paper notes that with mu = 0 'the maximum Sharpe ratio is equal to zero, implying that there is always a unique solution'. Since the engine sets mu = 0 (changed (9)) and alpha = 99% >> pi = 0.5%, the condition holds by construction and no runtime check is coded; the .RC_TOL acceptance test is what would catch a failure. (40) NO LIQUIDITY FILTER IN THE ENGINE: the paper states none for the factor application, so none is coded (paper_faithful); the axis hygiene membership separately carries a 20-day average turnover floor at t-1, disclosed by the harness in H1/H8.
paper_original_form: A 48-page asset-allocation paper: a risk budgeting (risk parity) portfolio over a handful of assets whose long-only fully-invested weights solve RC_i(x) = b_i ES_alpha(x) with ES taken under a 2-component Gaussian mixture; the empirical object is a 3-asset equity/bond/short-volatility mix (Jan 2000-Dec 2015, one-year rolling window, monthly rebalancing, normal-regime covariance from the A.9 filtering algorithm) plus section 5 illustrations over five long-only equity factors and over alternative risk premia. There is no cross-sectional stock selection anywhere in the paper.
declared_role: defensive (secondarily diversifier) - the abstract and section 4.3 claim that when assets exhibit jump risk the skewness-based risk parity portfolio 'produce[s] better allocation than volatility-based risk parity portfolios', i.e. it avoids over-allocating to assets whose losses arrive as jumps and 'remain[s] invested in skewed assets once the jump risk has been observed' (section 6); section 5.1 frames the equity-factor application as showing that 'the size and value allocation is generally overestimated in factor-based investing, because the portfolio construction does not take into account the skewness risk'. Paper wording only; no performance was consulted.

paper_steps.step: Return model: 2-component Gaussian mixture with a jump regime
paper_steps.paper_quote: f(y) = (1-pi) phi_3(y; mu dt, Sigma dt) + pi phi_3(y; mu dt + mu~, Sigma dt + Sigma~)  (eq.14, section 4.1)
paper_steps.note: engine.R section 2 (.sk_moments) builds the univariate mixture of x'R from (mu_1,Sigma_1) = (0, Sigma^_t) and (mu_2,Sigma_2) = (mu~, Sigma^_t + Sigma~); the same parametrisation is enforced inside the EM (engine.R section 5)

paper_steps.step: Portfolio return is itself a 2-component mixture
paper_steps.paper_quote: mu_1(x) = x'mu, sigma_1^2(x) = x'Sigma x, mu_2(x) = x'(mu + mu~), sigma_2^2(x) = x'(Sigma + Sigma~)x (section 2.2, eq.3)
paper_steps.note: engine.R .sk_moments returns m1, m2, s1, s2 and the two Sigma_j x products used by the gradient

paper_steps.step: Value-at-risk of the mixture as the root of the tail equation
paper_steps.paper_quote: (1-lambda) Phi((VaR_alpha(x)+mu_1(x))/sigma_1(x)) + lambda Phi((VaR_alpha(x)+mu_2(x))/sigma_2(x)) = alpha (section 3.1 / A.4); 'The calculation of the value-at-risk can then be done numerically using a bisection algorithm' (A.4)
paper_steps.note: engine.R .sk_var solves the algebraically identical complement form (1-lambda)Phi(-h_1)+lambda Phi(-h_2) = 1-alpha by uniroot on a bracketed strictly decreasing function; bracket widening declared in changed (23)

paper_steps.step: Expected shortfall under the mixture
paper_steps.paper_quote: ES_alpha(x) = (1-lambda) varphi(VaR_alpha(x), mu_1(x), sigma_1(x)) + lambda varphi(VaR_alpha(x), mu_2(x), sigma_2(x)), varphi(a,b,c) = (c/(1-alpha)) phi((a+b)/c) - (b/(1-alpha)) Phi(-(a+b)/c)  (eq.4)
paper_steps.note: engine.R .sk_risk: es = ((1-pi)(s1 phi(h1) - m1 Phi(-h1)) + pi (s2 phi(h2) - m2 Phi(-h2)))/(1-alpha), the A.4 closed form

paper_steps.step: Gradient of the value-at-risk
paper_steps.paper_quote: d_x VaR_alpha(x) = [varpi_1(x)((h_1/sigma_1)Sigma x - mu) + varpi_2(x)((h_2/sigma_2)(Sigma+Sigma~)x - (mu+mu~))] / (varpi_1(x)+varpi_2(x))  (A.5)
paper_steps.note: engine.R .sk_risk, object dvar, written literally

paper_steps.step: Marginal and total risk contributions
paper_steps.paper_quote: RC(x) = [varpi_1(x)/(1-alpha)](x o delta_1(x)) + [varpi_2(x)/(1-alpha)](x o delta_2(x)) - (1/(1-alpha))((1-lambda)(x o mu)Phi(-h_1(x)) + lambda(x o (mu+mu~))Phi(-h_2(x)))  (eq.5), with delta_1(x) = (1 + (h_1/sigma_1)VaR)Sigma x - VaR(d_x VaR + mu) and delta_2(x) = (1 + (h_2/sigma_2)VaR)(Sigma+Sigma~)x - VaR(d_x VaR + mu + mu~)  (A.5)
paper_steps.note: engine.R .sk_risk computes varpi_i, d_x VaR, delta_1, delta_2 and the eq.5 combination in the paper's own A.5 form (the previous rejected engine used a reduced re-expression; that is removed). RC = x o MR

paper_steps.step: Risk budgeting / risk parity equation
paper_steps.paper_quote: RC_i(x) = b_i R(x), b_i > 0, x_i >= 0, sum b_i = 1, sum x_i = 1  (eq.6)
paper_steps.note: engine.R .sk_solve; acceptance test max|RC_i/ES - b_i| <= .RC_TOL

paper_steps.step: Equal risk contribution budgets
paper_steps.paper_quote: We consider the equal risk contribution (ERC) portfolio where the risk budgets are the same for all the assets (section 3.3.2); 'The risk parity portfolio allocates the same volatility risk to the five risk factors' (section 5.1)
paper_steps.note: .RISK_BUDGET = rep(1/.N_SLEEVE, .N_SLEEVE) = 0.2 each; the paper gives no unequal b_i anywhere

paper_steps.step: Solve by the log-barrier program and renormalise
paper_steps.paper_quote: y* = arg min ES_alpha(y) - sum b_i ln y_i u.c. y >= 0; x*_i = y*_i / sum_j y*_j (section 3.3.2)
paper_steps.note: engine.R .sk_solve solves it in log coordinates y = exp(z) with the analytic gradient RC(exp z) - b; algorithm choice (BFGS), restarts and the no-fallback rule are declared in changed (22)-(23)

paper_steps.step: Existence and uniqueness condition
paper_steps.paper_quote: If alpha >= max(alpha^-, lambda), the RB portfolio exists and is unique (Theorem 1); 'in most cases, the vector of expected returns mu is equal to zero ... In this case, the maximum Sharpe ratio is equal to zero, implying that there is always a unique solution to the optimization program'
paper_steps.note: Satisfied by construction: mu = 0 so SR_1^+ = 0, and alpha = 99% >> pi = 0.5%. No runtime test is coded - declared in changed (39)

paper_steps.step: Long-only, fully invested constraints
paper_steps.paper_quote: sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i = 1 and x_i >= 0 (eq.6)
paper_steps.note: y = exp(z) enforces positivity; x = y/sum(y) enforces full investment; PORTFOLIO weights are renormalised to 1 after sleeve overlap is aggregated

paper_steps.step: Expected returns set to zero for the allocation
paper_steps.paper_quote: we assume that the expected returns mu_i are equal to zero and not to the historical estimates in order to limit the in-sample bias (section 4.2); 'the ERC portfolio is calculated by considering that the expected returns in the normal regime are equal to zero' (section 4.3 footnote)
paper_steps.note: .MU_NORMAL = 0 in the allocation; mu~ (the jump mean) is still estimated, so mu_2 = mu~. The filtering recursion keeps its own mu^_t for the posterior densities as A.9 step 2 requires - declared in changed (9)

paper_steps.step: Confidence level
paper_steps.paper_quote: We now calculate the ERC portfolio using the 99% expected shortfall risk measure (section 4.2); 'Recall that the risk measure corresponds to the 99% expected shortfall' (section 4.3 footnote)
paper_steps.note: .ES_ALPHA = 0.99

paper_steps.step: Jump probability calibrated, not estimated
paper_steps.paper_quote: we observe that the expected drawdown is about -10.5% for pi=0.5% when the return period is between 10 and 20 years (section 4.1); 'Moreover, we assume that pi is given in order to control the jump frequency'
paper_steps.note: .PI_JUMP = 0.005, the weekly-model value; pi is never updated in the M-step. Choice of the weekly cell is declared in changed (5); .N_MIN_JUMP = ceiling(1/pi) is derived from this same pi

paper_steps.step: EM estimation of the mixture parameters
paper_steps.paper_quote: E-step pi_{j,t}^(k) = pi_j^(k) phi_n(R_t; mu_j^(k), Sigma_j^(k)) / sum_s ...; M-step pi_j^(k+1) = sum_t pi_{j,t}/T, mu_j^(k+1) = sum_t pi_{j,t} R_t / sum_t pi_{j,t}, Sigma_j^(k+1) = sum_t pi_{j,t}(R_t - mu_j)(R_t - mu_j)' / sum_t pi_{j,t} (section 2.4, A.3 eq.17-20)
paper_steps.note: Implemented in engine.R .sk_em, but the paper specifies no initialisation, no iteration count and no convergence criterion, and its M-step updates pi whereas here pi stays at its calibrated value. Deterministic init, caps, tolerance, mass safeguards and ridges are declared in changed (12) and (24)

paper_steps.step: Jump covariance is a covariance matrix (parametrisation 14), no further structure
paper_steps.paper_quote: This parametrization ensures that the estimated model is a Gaussian mixture model with a jump component, and not a two-volatility regime model (section 4.1)
paper_steps.note: Enforced by projecting Sigma_2 - Sigma_1 onto the PSD cone inside every M-step and rebuilding component 2 as Sigma_1 + Sigma~; the constraint is the paper's, the projection mechanism is mine. Declared in changed (11)

paper_steps.step: Constraint: an asset whose expected jump is positive has no jump component
paper_steps.paper_quote: We also introduce the constraint that bonds have no jump component, because the previous estimations suggest that the expected jump is positive for this asset class. Moreover, it is not statistically significant. (section 4.1; Table 9 and Table 21 bonds row: mu~ = 0.00, sigma~ = 0.00, rho~ = 0.00; Tables 15-20 show the unconstrained bonds mu~ positive)
paper_steps.note: Implemented as a mechanical rule - any sleeve with mu~_i > 0 has mu~_i and row/column i of Sigma~ zeroed (engine.R .sk_zero_jump, .sk_jump_params). Not reproduced: the significance test, the paper's constrained MAXIMUM LIKELIHOOD re-estimation ('The EM algorithm can no longer be applied due to the constraints'), and the fixity of the constrained set. Declared in changed (10)

paper_steps.step: Backtest protocol: jump parameters fixed, normal-regime Sigma_t re-estimated on a one-year rolling window, monthly rebalancing
paper_steps.paper_quote: we assume that the parameters pi, mu~ and Sigma~ are given once and for all, and are set to the previous estimates. At each rebalancing date, we have to estimate the covariance matrix Sigma_t for the normal regime ... it is common to consider a monthly rebalancing based on a one-year rolling covariance matrix (section 4.3)
paper_steps.note: The split is kept (Sigma_t rolling and filtered, jump increments held between rebalancings) but the jump increments are re-estimated on an expanding window ending at each rebalancing date instead of the paper's full sample, because PIT C1 forbids full-sample statistics. Declared in changed (4) and (18)

paper_steps.step: Normal-regime Sigma_t by the filtering method: posterior jump probability per window date, then estimate from non-jump dates only
paper_steps.paper_quote: Given mu^_{t-1} and Sigma^_{t-1}, we estimate the jump probability for each dates of the rolling window that ends at time t; Given the previous jump probabilities, we estimate the parameters mu^_t and Sigma^_t by only considering the dates of the rolling window, which do not correspond to a jump [We use the rule pi^_t >= pi*]; We iterate the algorithm until today. (section 4.3). A.9 step 2: pi^_{t-s} = pi phi_n(y_{t-s}, mu^_{t-1}dt + mu~, Sigma^_{t-1}dt + Sigma~) / [(1-pi) phi_n(y_{t-s}, mu^_{t-1}dt, Sigma^_{t-1}dt) + pi phi_n(...)] for s = 0..n_rw-1; A.9 step 3: mu^_{i,t}dt = (1/n_t) sum_s 1{pi^_{t-s} <= pi_bar} y_{i,t-s}, Sigma^_{i,j,t}dt = (1/n_t) sum_s 1{pi^_{t-s} <= pi_bar}(y_{i,t-s}-mu^_{i,t})(y_{j,t-s}-mu^_{j,t}), n_t = sum_s 1{pi^_{t-s} <= pi_bar}
paper_steps.note: engine.R section 8: one forward pass over weeks, .sk_post_jump = A.9 step 2 (both components built from mu^_{t-1}, Sigma^_{t-1}), the keep mask and the n_t-divisor mean/covariance = A.9 step 3, iterated weekly = A.9 step 4. THIS IS THE STEP THE PREVIOUS REJECTED ENGINE OMITTED (it used cov() of the full 52-week window, i.e. the unconditional mixture covariance, which both inflated sigma_1 and double-counted the jump variance in sigma_2). The n_t floor and the warm-up regime are declared in changed (13)-(14)

paper_steps.step: Jump detection threshold
paper_steps.paper_quote: We will say that we observe a jump at time t when the posterior probability is larger than a threshold pi*: J_t = 1 <=> pi^_t >= pi* ... The out-of-sample probabilities correspond to the average of posterior probabilities, which are calculated using the filtering algorithm, a one-year rolling window and pi* = 30% (section 4.3)
paper_steps.note: .PI_STAR = 0.30; boundary convention declared in changed (15)

paper_steps.step: Initialisation of the filtering recursion
paper_steps.paper_quote: Let n_rw be the length of the rolling window. We initialize the filtering procedure at time n_rw + 1 (A.9 step 1); 'To initialize the algorithm, we can use the traditional Gaussian estimates' (A.9); 'The only difficulty is the initialization of the covariance matrix. For that, we consider that there is no jump in the first rolling window' (section 4.3)
paper_steps.note: At week 52 mu^ and Sigma^ are the Gaussian ML estimates of the first 52-week window and steps 2-3 start at week 53 = n_rw + 1; see also changed (14) for the warm-up span before any jump parameters exist

paper_steps.step: Maximum-likelihood alternative for Sigma_t
paper_steps.paper_quote: we can apply the method of maximum likelihood to the mixture model with the data of the rolling window ... However, estimating the covariance matrix in the normal regime by maximum likelihood is not our preferred approach
paper_steps.note: The paper names it only to reject it in favour of the filtering method, and reports the filtering allocation as the result (Figure 17). Declared in changed (16)

paper_steps.step: Thresholding jump detector (one- and multi-dimensional)
paper_steps.paper_quote: J_t = 1 <=> |R_t - v| >= r*; ... the thresholding approach is no longer valid in the multi-dimensional case ... For this reason, we prefer the filtering approach to detect jumps in the multi-dimensional case (section 4.3, A.7, A.8)
paper_steps.note: Explicitly rejected by the paper for the multivariate case, which is ours (n = 5). Declared in changed (33)

paper_steps.step: Allocated assets and sample: US bonds, S&P 500, short-volatility carry, Jan 2000 - Dec 2015
paper_steps.paper_quote: We use the Barclays US Government Bond Index, the S&P 500 TR Index and the generic equities/volatility/carry/US index calculated by Hamdan et al. (2016) ... for the study period January 2000-December 2015 (section 4)
paper_steps.note: Not reproducible - no US bond index and no short-volatility carry panel in this repository. Replaced by the paper's own section 5.1 assets. Declared in changed (1) and (3)

paper_steps.step: Section 5.1 assets: five long-only equity risk factors
paper_steps.paper_quote: It consists in building a diversified portfolio using the more relevant long-only equity risk factors (size, value, momentum, low beta and quality). This portfolio combines then two pure (or skewness) risk premia - size and value - and three market anomalies - momentum, low beta and quality (Cazalet and Roncalli, 2014)
paper_steps.note: Five sleeves, one per factor, via load_month_factors (see factor_mapping). This is the paper's own equity-factor application and is what the engine allocates over

paper_steps.step: Construction of the five factor portfolios themselves (universe, data source, index rules, weighting)
paper_steps.paper_quote: (none - section 5.1 is entirely qualitative: no table, no backtest, no universe, no exchange, no price or liquidity filter, no data source, no b_i assignment; the construction is delegated to Cazalet and Roncalli (2014))
paper_steps.note: The paper is silent, so our fixed axis supplies it: top-5 by Z_Score_Aligned, equal weight within sleeve, union at most 25 names. Declared in changed (6), with the leg-direction consequence in changed (8)

paper_steps.step: Pre-processing of the inputs (missing-value imputation, outlier treatment, standardisation, sector or market neutralisation)
paper_steps.paper_quote: (none - the paper allocates across already-built factor portfolios and states no cross-sectional pre-processing)
paper_steps.note: The paper has no such step, but Z_Score_Aligned is itself a winsorized, z-scored, direction-aligned, re-standardised value and that transform is therefore mine, not the paper's. Declared in changed (7)-(8); return-side missing handling in changed (19)

paper_steps.step: Cross-sectional sorting / quantile splits / independent sorts by market, exchange or sector
paper_steps.paper_quote: (none - the paper performs no cross-sectional security sort anywhere)
paper_steps.note: A single pooled cross-sectional ranking per factor over the whole hygiene universe, with no exchange or sector split. Declared in changed (6)

paper_steps.step: Comparison portfolios: minimum variance, minimum expected shortfall, Gaussian-model ERC
paper_steps.paper_quote: Table 11: Volatility and skewness risks of risk-based portfolios (weekly model) - minimum variance, equal risk contribution and minimum expected shortfall portfolios across Gaussian and mixture models
paper_steps.note: Diagnostic comparisons in the paper, not the framework portfolio. Only the mixture ERC portfolio is implemented. Declared in changed (33)

paper_steps.step: Cornish-Fisher / skewness-adjusted VaR
paper_steps.paper_quote: Another approach consists in using the Cornish-Fisher value-at-risk. Again, this approach is not used in practice because it requires the computation of co-skewness statistics, which are difficult to estimate (section 1)
paper_steps.note: The paper explicitly rejects this route in favour of mixture ES, so nothing to implement

paper_steps.step: Transaction costs
paper_steps.paper_quote: (mentioned only as motivation - 'This is particularly true if we consider transaction costs' (section 5 opening) - and never modelled; section 4.4 reports turnover 53.19% vs 31.45%, not costs)
paper_steps.note: commission_paper = null; only the harness 15bps grade board applies (H7). Declared in changed (34)

paper_steps.step: Liquidity / tradability filter
paper_steps.paper_quote: (none - the paper states no liquidity rule for the equity factor application)
paper_steps.note: paper_faithful: the engine adds no liquidity filter. The axis hygiene membership separately carries a 20-day average turnover floor at t-1, which the harness discloses in H1/H8 and which the engine does not duplicate. Declared in changed (40)

windows.name: Sigma^_t rolling window (A.9 filtering, normal regime)
windows.paper: A.9 steps 2-3, s = 0..n_rw-1 over y_{t-s} with n_rw = one year of weekly returns, i.e. weeks [t-51, t] INCLUSIVE of t, with the jump dates (pi^ > pi_bar) removed before the mean and covariance are formed and n_t = the number of kept dates as divisor
windows.impl: rows (t-51):t of the completed weekly sleeve-return panel, i.e. weeks [t-51, t] inclusive of t, where t = the last week that CLOSED at or before the signal date d (any week still running past d is excluded); keep mask 1{pi^ <= .PI_STAR}, divisor n_t = number of kept weeks (ML divisor). If n_t < .MIN_OBS_COV = 6 the previous (mu^, Sigma^) are carried unchanged

windows.name: Filtering recursion span
windows.paper: A.9 step 1: initialise at time n_rw + 1; step 4: iterate until today
windows.impl: single forward pass over weeks t = 52..T of the weekly panel; t = 52 is the Gaussian ML initialisation (window [1,52], nothing excluded), t >= 53 = n_rw+1 runs A.9 steps 2-3 using (mu^_{t-1}, Sigma^_{t-1}); weeks 53..199 have no jump parameters yet and therefore exclude nothing (changed (14))

windows.name: Jump increments mu~, Sigma~ (EM window)
windows.paper: full sample, estimated once and then 'given once and for all' for the whole backtest
windows.impl: EXPANDING window = every complete weekly sleeve return with week-ending day <= the signal date, endpoint = that week inclusive, minimum .N_MIN_JUMP = 200 weeks; refreshed once per rebalancing week AFTER that week's filter update, and held fixed in between. Endpoint differs from the paper (paper = whole sample including the future); changed (4) and (18)

windows.name: EM jump-component initialisation slice
windows.impl: the k2 = max(.EM_INIT_JUMP_OBS = 6, floor(pi*T)) most negative equal-weight weeks of the SAME expanding window [1, t], endpoint = week t inclusive; deterministic, no RNG

windows.name: Weekly return compounding window
windows.paper: weekly returns (frequency only; no indexing convention given)
windows.impl: ISO Monday-to-Sunday blocks keyed by (as.integer(Date) - .WEEK_ANCHOR) %/% .WEEK_LEN with .WEEK_ANCHOR = 4 (1970-01-05, a Monday) and .WEEK_LEN = 7; a week's return = prod(1+Ret)-1 over that week's trading days, endpoint = the week's last trading day

windows.name: Sleeve composition as-of window
windows.paper: (not applicable - the paper's assets are pre-built factor portfolios with no composition step)
windows.impl: the composition priced during ISO week w is the one formed at the latest month-end signal date STRICTLY BEFORE w's first trading day (findInterval on wstart - .ASOF_LAG_DAYS, .ASOF_LAG_DAYS = 1), endpoint = that month-end; no week is ever priced with a composition chosen during or after it

windows.name: Signal date grid
windows.impl: the last trading day of each calendar month in RAWDATA with Date >= .RP_START_DATE, endpoint = that month-end inclusive; exactly one signal per month, so the harness takes the monthly path (H10)

windows.name: Daily return window (Close fallback only)
windows.paper: (none - the paper consumes index return series directly)
windows.impl: Ret = Close/shift(Close, .RET_LAG_DAYS)-1 per ticker over consecutive available trading days, endpoint = day t vs the previous available day; used only when RAWDATA carries no Ret column

windows.name: Factor-DB internal windows (not computed by this engine)
windows.paper: (none - the paper specifies no factor construction window)
windows.impl: inherited from the registry through load_month_factors: 252-day cumulative return with a 1-month skip (M01_Mom_12_1), 252-day rolling CAPM beta (D02_Beta), quarterly+45d / annual 3/31 fundamental availability (V01_BM, Q01_GPA), T-1 for rawdata-sourced factors; endpoints governed by the connector's lag_rule Date <= sig_d and by the monthly panel's own asof date (<= signal date, enforced in the engine). The ic_sign direction comes from an expanding IC window with a 36-month burn-in and Usable_Date <= sig_date. Declared in changed (8) and (31)

factor_mapping.paper_item: the 'size' long-only equity risk factor of section 5.1 (one of the 'two pure (or skewness) risk premia - size and value')
factor_mapping.registry_definition: -log(MarketCap). Log negative market cap for size premium.
factor_mapping.deviation: The paper names the factor but never defines or constructs it, so the metric and its lag (T-1, rawdata) come from the registry rather than the paper. The consumed value is Z_Score_Aligned, i.e. cross-sectionally winsorized, z-scored, re-standardised to sd = 1, and direction-aligned by the connector's ic_sign (expanding-window IC first, registry direction only as fallback) - so the sleeve is a small-cap leg only while the realised IC sign agrees with the registry's higher_better; it can invert. See changed (8). Registry dedup cluster DUPC-030 (partners L26_Log_MktCap, S02_Float_Size); neither partner is used.

factor_mapping.paper_item: the 'value' long-only equity risk factor of section 5.1
factor_mapping.registry_definition: TotalEquity / MarketCap. Ratio of book value to market capitalization.
factor_mapping.deviation: Paper names but does not define the factor; book-to-market is the registry's canonical value metric. Availability rule quarterly+45d;annual_3/31 (C4) is the registry's, not the paper's. Consumed as Z_Score_Aligned with the ic_sign-driven direction described in changed (8). No dedup declaration in the registry, so no cluster conflict.

factor_mapping.paper_item: the 'momentum' long-only equity risk factor of section 5.1 (one of the 'three market anomalies')
factor_mapping.registry_definition: 252-day cumulative return with 1-month skip. Classic 12-1 momentum signal.
factor_mapping.deviation: The 252-day window and the 1-month skip are registry choices; the paper specifies no momentum horizon and no skip. Consumed as Z_Score_Aligned with the ic_sign-driven direction described in changed (8). Registry dedup cluster DUPC-032 (partner M13_VolAdj_Mom); the partner is not used.

factor_mapping.paper_item: the 'low beta' long-only equity risk factor of section 5.1 (one of the 'three market anomalies')
factor_mapping.registry_definition: CAPM beta coefficient (252d rolling). Market sensitivity.
factor_mapping.deviation: The 252-day estimation window is the registry's, not the paper's. The registry direction is lower_better, which would orient high Z_Score_Aligned = LOW beta as the paper's leg requires, BUT the registry is only the connector's second branch: Z_Score_Aligned = Z_Score * ic_sign with ic_sign taken from the expanding-window mean IC whenever that IC exists (36-month burn-in). In periods whose realised IC for beta is positive this sleeve is a HIGH-beta sleeve, not the paper's low-beta leg. This is NOT a guarantee and is declared as a deviation in changed (8); PIT C13 forbids the engine from imposing the sign itself. Registry dedup cluster DUPC-011 (partners D10_Blume_Adj_Beta, D11_FP_Beta, D18_BAB_Rank, D19_EW_Beta_63, D20_EW_Beta_126, D28_Unlevered_Beta, D31_Relative_Beta, MK01_CAPM_Beta); none of them is used.

factor_mapping.paper_item: the 'quality' long-only equity risk factor of section 5.1 (one of the 'three market anomalies')
factor_mapping.deviation: Paper names but does not define 'quality'; gross-profits-to-assets is the registry's canonical quality metric and the choice among several quality candidates (Q02_ROE, Q03_ROA) is mine. Availability rule quarterly+45d;annual_3/31 (C4) is the registry's. Consumed as Z_Score_Aligned with the ic_sign-driven direction described in changed (8). No dedup declaration in the registry, so no cluster conflict.

constants.name: .PI_JUMP
constants.note: section 4.1 weekly model jump probability pi = 0.5%, calibrated by matching the expected drawdown ('the expected drawdown is about -10.5% for pi=0.5% when the return period is between 10 and 20 years'); the monthly cell is 1.0% (Table 21) and was not taken - see changed (5)

constants.name: .ES_ALPHA
constants.note: section 4.2 'the ERC portfolio using the 99% expected shortfall risk measure'; section 4.3 footnote 'the risk measure corresponds to the 99% expected shortfall'

constants.name: .N_WIN_NORMAL
constants.note: section 4.3 'a one-year rolling covariance matrix' / A.9 n_rw, expressed in the weekly return frequency of the weekly model

constants.name: .PI_STAR
constants.note: section 4.3 'the filtering algorithm, a one-year rolling window and pi* = 30%'; used both as the jump rule J_t = 1 <=> pi^_t >= pi* and as A.9 step 3's pi_bar

constants.name: .MU_NORMAL
constants.note: section 4.2 'we assume that the expected returns mu_i are equal to zero and not to the historical estimates in order to limit the in-sample bias'

constants.name: .DT
constants.note: Remark 1 'Without loss of generality, we set dt equal to one in the sequel'; it multiplies mu^ and Sigma^ in the A.9 posterior so the correspondence with phi_n(y; mu^ dt, Sigma^ dt) stays visible, and drops out of every other formula - see changed (17)

constants.name: .TOP_N_SLEEVE
constants.note: paper gives no sleeve size; 25-name axis cap divided by the paper's 5 factors, so the union of sleeves is always <= 25

constants.name: .MIN_SLEEVE_NAMES
constants.note: minimum ranked candidates for a sleeve to be considered to exist (also the universe-size floor); below it the whole month is skipped rather than allocated over fewer than five sleeves (the paper's n is fixed at 5). Defence code, not in the paper

constants.name: .FDB_COVERAGE_MIN
constants.note: load_month_factors() default coverage floor, passed explicitly instead of relied upon; the paper has no coverage requirement

constants.name: .WEEK_ANCHOR
constants.note: day number of 1970-01-05, a Monday; used only to key ISO Monday-to-Sunday week blocks without a locale-dependent strftime %G-%V

constants.name: .WEEK_LEN
constants.note: days per ISO week block in the same keying expression; calendar fact, not a tunable parameter. Lifted out of the code as an inline literal - changed (38)

constants.name: .ASOF_LAG_DAYS
constants.note: the composition in force during a week is the one formed at the latest month-end STRICTLY before that week's first trading day; implemented as findInterval(wstart - 1, month_ends). PIT rule of mine, the paper has no composition step - changed (38)

constants.name: .RET_LAG_DAYS
constants.note: daily return lag Close/shift(Close, 1)-1, used only when RAWDATA carries no Ret column; structural, not in the paper - changed (19), (38)

constants.name: .COV_RIDGE
constants.note: relative diagonal ridge on every filtered covariance (Sigma^_t and Sigma^_t + Sigma~); numerical guard, not in the paper

constants.name: .EM_RIDGE
constants.note: relative diagonal ridge on the EM component covariances so the Cholesky in the log-density survives a near-singular jump component; numerical guard, not in the paper

constants.name: .EM_MAX_ITER
constants.note: the paper states no iteration cap ('the EM algorithm generally converges')

constants.name: .EM_TOL
constants.note: the paper states no convergence criterion; applied to the maximum change in posterior probabilities

constants.name: .EM_MIN_JUMP_MASS
constants.note: minimum effective posterior mass (in observations) for an M-step to be accepted; below it the loop breaks and the last valid parameters are kept. Guards against total collapse of the jump component (and against the unbounded-likelihood spike of a 1-observation component); not in the paper, and at pi = 0.5% it often ends the EM after one M-step - changed (12)

constants.name: .VAR_BRACKET_MULT
constants.note: VaR root bracket half-width = max|mu_j| + 20 * max(sigma_j); numerical, not in the paper (which only says 'a bisection algorithm', A.4)

constants.name: .VAR_BRACKET_TRIES
constants.note: maximum bracket widening attempts before returning NA; numerical, not in the paper

constants.name: .VAR_BRACKET_GROWTH
constants.note: geometric growth factor of the bracket widening step; numerical, not in the paper

constants.name: .VAR_TOL
constants.note: uniroot tolerance for the mixture VaR equation; numerical, not in the paper

constants.name: .OPT_MAXIT
constants.note: BFGS iteration cap on the log-barrier program; the paper names the program (section 3.3.2) but no algorithm

constants.name: .OPT_RELTOL
constants.note: BFGS relative tolerance; numerical, not in the paper

constants.name: .OPT_PENALTY
constants.note: 1e10, the objective value returned when a trial step makes ES non-finite or non-positive so BFGS steps back; numerical, not in the paper

constants.name: .OPT_RESTARTS
constants.note: number of starting points tried (inverse-volatility, then equal weight) before the month is abandoned; not in the paper

constants.name: .RC_TOL
constants.note: maximum |RC_i/ES - b_i| accepted as a solved risk budgeting problem; above it from every start the month emits nothing (no model-switching fallback). Acceptance test is mine, not the paper's

constants.name: .NUM_FLOOR
constants.note: variance and denominator floor, used as sqrt(max(x'Sigma x, floor)) and pmax(diag(Sigma), floor); numerical guard, not in the paper

constants.name: .VARPI_FLOOR
constants.note: floor on varpi_1(x) + varpi_2(x), the denominator of the A.5 value-at-risk gradient; below it the gradient is declared unevaluable and the optimisation attempt is abandoned (changed (23)). Numerical guard, not in the paper

constants.name: .FACTOR_IDS
constants.note: the five factor NAMES are the paper's (section 5.1 'size, value, momentum, low beta and quality'); the specific registry ids that realise them are mine because the paper gives no construction - see factor_mapping

constants.name: .N_SLEEVE
constants.note: length(.FACTOR_IDS); the paper's section 5.1 portfolio has exactly these five factors

constants.name: .RISK_BUDGET
constants.note: rep(1/.N_SLEEVE, .N_SLEEVE); the paper's equal risk contribution budgets b_i = 1/n (section 3.3.2, section 5.1 'allocates the same ... risk to the five risk factors')

constants.name: .N_MIN_JUMP
constants.note: as.integer(ceiling(1/.PI_JUMP)) weeks - the shortest expanding window in which the jump regime has at least one expected observation (pi*T >= 1). Derived from the paper's pi, but the minimum-window requirement itself is mine, imposed because the paper's full-sample jump estimation is not PIT-admissible. This is what creates the roughly 3.9-year warm-up with no output; changed (3) and (4)

constants.name: .EM_INIT_JUMP_OBS
constants.note: .N_SLEEVE + 1 - floor on the deterministic EM initialisation slice k2 = max(6, floor(pi*T)), being the minimum observation count for a non-singular 5x5 covariance. Not in the paper

constants.name: .MIN_OBS_COV
constants.note: .N_SLEEVE + 1 - minimum observations for a non-singular 5x5 covariance, used as (a) the A.9 n_t floor, (b) the EM normal-regime mass floor, (c) the EM minimum window length offset. Not in the paper

[HARNESS-DISCLOSURE v1]
- H1 유니버스: 측정 축 = 전 종목 + 위생(epoch all_hyg_2000_v1). 계약(contracts/measurement_axis.R::ma_inject_universe)이 적재 직후 RAWDATA 의 K200 플래그를 위생 멤버십(1/0)으로 바꿔 끼우고 KQ150 은 0 으로 둔다. 위생 멤버 = 20일 평균 거래대금(종가 × 거래량 · 하루 늦춤 t−1) ≥ 200,000,000원 ∧ 관리종목 · 거래정지 · 불성실공시 표식 아님(퀀티와이즈 월말 스냅샷을 다음 스냅샷까지 이월 — 그날까지 알려진 값만). 엔진 산출(FACTORS·PORTFOLIO)은 각 신호일의 이 멤버십과 결합되어 그날 비멤버 행이 제거된다 — PIT 시변 · 사후 생존 조건 없음 · 상장폐지 종목 포함(폐지 뒤 수익 행 부재 = 0 · 행이 없는 날 = 비멤버).
- H2 지수 플래그: 원래 지수 멤버십(KOSPI200 · KOSDAQ150)은 K200_IDX · KQ150_IDX 열에 보존된다 — 이 축에서 K200 · KQ150 플래그는 지수 멤버십이 아니다(K200 = 위생 멤버 · KQ150 = 0).
- H3 표본: 신호는 .RP_START_DATE(2000-01-01) 이후만 측정한다. 성과는 실효 시작부터 센다 — 실효 시작 = 신호 폭(유니버스 결합 뒤 점수가 유한한 종목 수 · 엔진이 SIGNAL_BREADTH 를 내면 그 값) ≥ 보유 수 × 2 를 처음 만족한 신호일(MC3 B안 · 첫 통과 = PIT). 그 전 신호일은 측정에서 빠진다(측정 축 규약 · 엔진 변경 아님). PORTFOLIO 만 내는 엔진은 폭을 잴 수 없어 자르지 않는다. 논문 표본기간과 다르다.
- H4 체결: 신호일 d 에 확정한 비중을 다음 거래일 종가에 체결(close_t1) — 새 보유 수익은 집행 다음 날부터 다음 집행일까지, 집행일 당일 수익은 직전 보유(동일봉 체결 없음).
- H5 보유: 연속한 두 신호일의 집행 사이 보유창 안에서 buy-and-hold(비중 드리프트) — 다음 신호일 집행 때 목표비중으로 되돌린다. 어떤 달에 엔진 산출이 없으면 그 달은 리밸이 없어 직전 보유가 다음 신호까지 이월된다.
- H6 비중: FACTORS 면 portfolio_spec(top_n_long 등)으로 신호일마다 유니버스 결합 뒤 점수 순 구성 · PORTFOLIO 면 유니버스 결합 뒤 남은 비중을 그대로 쓴다 — 빠진 종목 몫은 재분배되지 않아 그 다리 총노출이 줄어든다(현금처럼 0 수익). 롱·숏 다리 결합 = GL·L − GS·S(GL·GS = 다리 Σ|w|).
- H7 비용: 등급판 = 리밸마다 Σ|Δw|×15bps(초기 매수 = Σ|w|) · 논문판 = commission_paper(무명시면 0)로 병기한다.
- H8 유동성: 러너는 별도 유동성 필터를 걸지 않는다(paper_faithful). 다만 H1 의 위생 멤버십이 20일 평균 거래대금 200,000,000원(t−1) 하한을 이미 포함한다 — 논문에 유동성 규칙이 있으면 엔진이 논문대로 건다(위생 하한과 겹칠 수 있다).
- H9 벤치마크: KOSPI200.
- H10 리밸 주기: 엔진 신호일이 어느 달이든 둘 이상이면 주간 경로 — 신호 다음 거래일 집행 · ISO 주마다 마지막 신호 1개 · 그 신호일 거래량 0 종목 제외 뒤 다리 안 재정규화. 일간 신호는 주간으로 접히고 계약이 FIDELITY 에 자동 신고한다(일간 집행은 지원하지 않는다 — D16). 모든 달이 신호 1개 이하면 월간 경로(익월 첫 거래일 집행).
[/HARNESS-DISCLOSURE]
